lives only in one partner's head protects nothing.**

This file is self-contained on purpose: a teammate who clones only this repo has everything
they need. (Nick has a separate personal course-notes folder one level up; that is not team law
and is not required to work in this repo.)

---

## Project status (update this as things get decided)

- **Idea: LOCKED — Dark Sky Monitor.** An offline device that measures sky brightness and cloud
  cover at one site and grades the night GOOD / MARGINAL / POOR / UNKNOWN with the evidence behind
  the verdict. Full design review in [`docs/design-review.md`](docs/design-review.md).
- **Team:** Nick Marechal + Liam Sagal.
- **Where we left off: [`docs/progress-log.md`](docs/progress-log.md). Read it first.** Newest
  entry on top: milestone position, what code exists and what it guarantees, the shared record
  contract, and the open work. Add an entry there when you finish a chunk of work.
- **Hardware: two kits.** **`darksky.local`** (Nick: Pi 4 Model B **1 GB** + TSL2591 + MLX90614
  **3.3 V** + BME280; arrived 2026-10-13, set up headless 2026-10-27, I2C on, power `0x0`) is the
  **device of record**: the soak, the demo and every evaluation number come only from it.
  **`starlight.local`** (Liam's dev Pi + the same three sensors) is for parallel development only.
  **No sensors wired on either kit yet.** DS3231 RTC ordered 2026-10-27; until it is fitted the Pi
  takes real time from the network at boot. Enclosure still unbought. See
  [`docs/hardware-log.md`](docs/hardware-log.md) and [`docs/bill-of-materials.md`](docs/bill-of-materials.md).
- **Mechanisms: D** (crash-consistent storage) **+ E** (multiprocess + IPC + supervisor). C and F
  were considered and rejected — at 0.1–1 Hz sampling neither is justified, and being able to say
  why is a stronger defense answer than bolting them on.
- **Next action:** wire the sensors and run the bring-up checklist in
  [`docs/hardware-log.md`](docs/hardware-log.md) (M2: "both sensors electrically alive"). Step 4
  (acrylic vs. LDPE film in front of the MLX90614) tests the largest hardware unknown in the
  project. `DESIGN.md` (M2) is still unwritten.
- **Open gap:** the problem memo names an archetype, not a named individual. Outreach to the
  Northern Colorado Astronomical Society / CSU astronomy faculty still pending.

## Commands

- Build: `make`            Deploy to Pi: `make deploy PI=pi@<host>`
- Tests: `make test`       Sanitizers: `make asan`      Valgrind: `make memcheck`
- Soak sanity: `make soakcheck` (1-hour miniature of the 48h run)
- **A change is DONE only when build, test, and asan pass. Show the output.**

Targets exist and run today; several are no-ops until there is source to build. Do not let a
target silently become a lie — if it stops doing what its name says, fix it or rename it.

## Hard constraints (graded — spec §3.3, §3.4)

- The PRODUCT makes **no network calls except serving its own LAN interface**. No LLM APIs, no
  cloud inference, no pretrained models, no external weather/data APIs at runtime. The device
  must work with the network cable unplugged. The intelligence in `analysis/` is ours. A grader
  must be able to confirm this in one minute by reading the source tree.
  - Public data (NWS, USGS, etc.) may be used **only** as an offline ground-truth comparison
    while writing the evaluation report — never called from the device's own code.
- Every daemon must be **supervisable**: clean exit codes, no orphaned fds across restart,
  heartbeat within 60s of start.
- Every allocation checked; every syscall's error path handled and logged. The 48-hour soak is
  the test suite of last resort.
- **NEVER weaken, skip, or delete a test to make the suite pass.**
- Replayed or synthesized data is **labeled as such everywhere it appears** — in logs, in the
  report, in the demo. The 48h soak and the live demo run on live sensors.

## Style

- Systems core: **C17, `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, no VLAs.** `goto`-cleanup for multi-resource
  functions. ASan/valgrind findings cap that component's score at 50%, so they are bugs, not
  warnings.
- Python permitted only under `tools/` and `ui/`. **No graded mechanism may live there.**
- Smallest diff that passes. Do not refactor unrelated code.

## Ownership

Ownership means **first authorship and answerability at the defense**, not exclusivity. Each
partner is individually examined on their own subsystems plus one question from across the
boundary.

- **Nick:** `src/common/` (record format + CRC — owned by storage, used by everyone) and
  `src/store/` — mechanism **D**, the crash-consistent storage layer.
- **Liam (proposed — Liam to confirm):** `src/super/`, `src/sensors/`, and the IPC — mechanism
  **E**, the supervisor and the sensor daemons. All Linux-only I2C code lives in `src/sensors/`,
  so everything else builds and tests on a Mac.
- **To decide together:** analysis (ephemeris, features, classifier, state machine) and the
  query CLI.
- The agent edits outside the current session owner's area only when told explicitly whose
  session this is.

## Workflow (spec §10, Assignment 0's nine steps apply verbatim)

- Multi-file or algorithmic change: **plan first, wait for approval.** No code in the first pass.
- **Hardware bugs: paste real evidence** — `dmesg`, timing captures, `/proc/interrupts`, logic
  analyzer output. Never propose or accept a fix derived from a verbal description of a sensor
  problem. The agent will confidently reason about a sensor it has never met and be wrong in
  ways only an instrument catches.
- Commit only from a green state; message format `M<n>: <what>`.
- **≥ 40 meaningful commits** across the project, both partners well represented. A pair of
  "final submission" commits is an automatic process grade of **zero, for both partners.**

  shared login defeats the per-partner transcript grading and costs both of you.
- Every milestone's diffs get **two reviews**: a fresh-context agent review and a human review
  by the partner who did not write the code. Each partner's `PROMPTLOG.md` must record at least
  one review of the other's work.

## Transcript discipline (do not skip — spec §6, §10.4)

At **every** milestone M1–M5, each partner copies their raw `.jsonl` sessions from
`~/.claude/projects/<project-dir>/` into `transcripts/<partner>/`. As-is. Not summarized, not
exported, not retyped. See `transcripts/README.md`.

Losing Week-5 transcripts in Week 15 is a foreseeable loss, and foreseeable losses are not
excused.

## 2026-10-27 (evening) — M2 design document written (Liam)

Nick was unavailable, so Liam wrote `DESIGN.md` alone for the M2 deadline (2026-10-28, Canvas
date). The course handout was read in full and is kept locally only (`docs/CS370-TermProject.pdf`,
git-ignored).

### What changed

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `f85b220` | `.gitignore` the handout PDF |
| `4a75922` | DESIGN: architecture diagram with a rate on every arrow |
| `4deb2f6` | DESIGN: mechanism mapping. E: R-E1 (UNKNOWN within 60 s), R-E2 (≤ 10 s lost per crash). D: R-D1 (≤ 60 s lost per power cut), R-D2 (20/20 recoveries), R-D3 (≥ 180 days on 16 GB) |
| `584ac8b` | DESIGN: failure-mode table (13 rows, each with how to inject it) and storage |
| `32a55e8` | New [`record-and-ipc.md`](record-and-ipc.md): record layout, payloads, rate derivation, ring invariants, channels, supervision rules |
| `9fa7f0b` | DESIGN: constraints and evaluation plan (14 rows, each with a numeric target) |
| `b053730` | DESIGN: ownership, AI-use plan, trimmed to 5 pages |
| this commit | `CLAUDE.md`, hardware log, this entry |

### How it was verified

- On a CS department Linux machine (x86-64, gcc 16.1.0), **not the Pi**: `make` exit 0;
  `make test` 116 checks, 0 failed; `make asan` 116 checks, 0 failed; `make clean && make
  memcheck` 0 errors, no leaks.
- `DESIGN.md` is 5 pages rendered by pandoc → PDF (xelatex, 11 pt, 1-inch margins, US letter).
  The handout sets no format; this is the measure we used.
- `grep -rnE 'AF_INET|PF_INET|getaddrinfo|gethostbyname|curl|https?://' src/` prints nothing.

### Decisions marked "proposed (Liam), Nick to confirm" (‡ in DESIGN.md)

1. **Hub → storage:** `AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET`, one record per message. `stored` accepts
   `fusiond` and `dskyd` and stays the only writer. While `stored` is down, `fusiond` buffers 4096
   records (≈ 50 min), then drops the oldest and counts.
2. **Durability:** `write()` every 10 s or 64 records; `fsync()` every 60 s, at rotation and at
   shutdown; directory `fsync()` after creating a segment.
3. **Segments:** one per night, rotated at local noon (every 24 h of monotonic time when the clock
   is unsynced), 32 MB cap. No MANIFEST: recovery scans only the open segment.
4. **Retention:** raw 180 days, rollups forever; raw writes stop below 2 GB free.
5. **Torn header:** a 1–23-byte file with our segment name in our data directory is recreated; any
   other short file is still refused.
6. **`seq` per (source, run):** a new kind START (= 6) opens every run, carrying the run number
   from `dskyd`.
7. **Failures in records:** an I/O failure is a FAULT (the first, then ≤ 1 per 60 s); an
   implausible value is a SAMPLE without `VALID`.
8. **`source_id`s:** 0 reserved, 1 `skyd`, 2 `cloudd`, 3 `envd`, 4 `fusiond`, 5 `dskyd`,
   6 `stored`.
9. **Payloads:** Nick's SAMPLE table adopted as is; FEATURE, STATE, HEARTBEAT, FAULT and START
   added; new flag `CLOCK_UNSYNC` = bit 4. No layout change. See `record-and-ipc.md`.
10. **Analysis split:** Liam takes the classifier + state machine; Nick takes features,
    ephemeris and `dsq`.
11. **Evaluation targets in Nick's area:** row 2 (durable p99 ≤ 61 s), 10 (`fsync` sweep, ≤ 30
    MB/day written at 60 s), 11 (power cut 20/20, ≤ 60 s lost), 12 (ephemeris ≤ 0.1° sun, ≤ 0.5°
    moon).

### Decided in Liam's area (mechanism E)

Three sensor daemons share the bus; an I2C broker is the fallback if p99 interval jitter > 100 ms.
Shared-memory single-producer/single-consumer rings, chosen for decoupled lifetimes. One thread
per process. A hang is detected after 20 s of a silent liveness pipe. A "sensor absent" exit code
→ `DEAD` + re-probe every 60 s. Crash backoff 1 → 60 s; 5 crashes in 300 s → `DEAD`. systemd
supervises `dskyd`; children use `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`. Hourly heartbeat; stderr → journald. No IP
sockets. With no RTC: `CLOCK_UNSYNC` flag and an UNKNOWN verdict.

### Hardware

- **Two kits.** `darksky.local` (Nick) is the device of record: soak, demo and every evaluation
  number. `starlight.local` (Liam: Pi $45 + sensors $32 = $77) is for development only. Team
  ≈ $145 against the handout's $50–80 guideline, before the unrecorded PSUs, SD cards, RTC and
  enclosure.
- DS3231 ordered 2026-10-27 (Liam).
- **No sensor wired on either kit.** "Both sensors electrically alive" was not met for M2; target
  2026-11-03 for hardware-log §1–5 on `darksky.local`.

### Open

- **Nick:** confirm or change items 1–11 above, then review the DESIGN.md diffs (that review is
  the PROMPTLOG cross-review episode).
- **Liam:** write up a review of Nick's `src/store/` and `src/common/` in `PROMPTLOG-liam.md`.
  Findings so far: a 1–23-byte file is refused forever (item 5 addresses it), no directory
  `fsync` after create, and `seq` resets on restart (item 6 addresses it).
- **Both:** copy out M2 transcripts to `transcripts/<name>/2026-10-27-m2/`.
- **Makefile bug, not fixed:** `make memcheck` straight after `make asan` runs valgrind on the
  ASan binary and crashes. Run `make clean` first. `vgcore.*` is also missing from `.gitignore`.
- **Docs that still contradict the design:**
  - README says the Pi isn't ordered and the project is at M0.
  - The BOM's Decisions section says Pi 4 2 GB, "buy Adafruit" and a 32 GB high-endurance card;
    we have 1 GB, clones and a standard 16 GB card. It also argues for both a narrow and a wide
    field of view.
  - `design-review.md` says the project can't work without an RTC.
  - `transcripts/README.md` names `liam/2026-09-23-m1/`; the folder is `m0-m1`.
- **Prices not recorded:** PSUs, SD cards, card reader (both kits).
- **Commits after this one:** 26 in total, Liam 9 (≈ 35 %).

### How it was verified

- On a CS department Linux machine (x86-64, gcc 16.1.0), **not the Pi**: `make` exit 0;

  memcheck` 0 errors, no leaks.

### Decisions marked "proposed (Liam), Nick to confirm" (‡ in DESIGN.md)

1. **Hub → storage:** `AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET`, one record per message. `stored` accepts
   `fusiond` and `dskyd` and stays the only writer. While `stored` is down, `fusiond` buffers 4096
   records (≈ 50 min), then drops the oldest and counts.
2. **Durability:** `write()` every 10 s or 64 records; `fsync()` every 60 s, at rotation and at
   shutdown; directory `fsync()` after creating a segment.
3. **Segments:** one per night, rotated at local noon (every 24 h of monotonic time when the clock
   is unsynced), 32 MB cap. No MANIFEST: recovery scans only the open segment.
4. **Retention:** raw 180 days, rollups forever; raw writes stop below 2 GB free.
5. **Torn header:** a 1–23-byte file with our segment name in our data directory is recreated; any
   other short file is still refused.
6. **`seq` per (source, run):** a new kind START (= 6) opens every run, carrying the run number
   from `dskyd`.
7. **Failures in records:** an I/O failure is a FAULT (the first, then ≤ 1 per 60 s); an
   implausible value is a SAMPLE without `VALID`.
8. **`source_id`s:** 0 reserved, 1 `skyd`, 2 `cloudd`, 3 `envd`, 4 `fusiond`, 5 `dskyd`,
   6 `stored`.
9. **Payloads:** Nick's SAMPLE table adopted as is; FEATURE, STATE, HEARTBEAT, FAULT and START
   added; new flag `CLOCK_UNSYNC` = bit 4. No layout change. See `record-and-ipc.md`.
10. **Analysis split:** Liam takes the classifier + state machine; Nick takes features,
    ephemeris and `dsq`.
11. **Evaluation targets in Nick's area:** row 2 (durable p99 ≤ 61 s), 10 (`fsync` sweep, ≤ 30
    MB/day written at 60 s), 11 (power cut 20/20, ≤ 60 s lost), 12 (ephemeris ≤ 0.1° sun, ≤ 0.5°
    moon).

### Decided in Liam's area (mechanism E)

Three sensor daemons share the bus; an I2C broker is the fallback if p99 interval jitter > 100 ms.
Shared-memory single-producer/single-consumer rings, chosen for decoupled lifetimes. One thread
per process. A hang is detected after 20 s of a silent liveness pipe. A "sensor absent" exit code
→ `DEAD` + re-probe every 60 s. Crash backoff 1 → 60 s; 5 crashes in 300 s → `DEAD`. systemd
supervises `dskyd`; children use `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`. Hourly heartbeat; stderr → journald. No IP
sockets. With no RTC: `CLOCK_UNSYNC` flag and an UNKNOWN verdict.
